items.title: A proper morphism with finite fibre over a one dimensional point is finite over a neighbourhood
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a proper morphism f: X to Y and a point y whose local ring is Noetherian of dimension at most one, under any of the listed hypotheses at generic points of X, the lemma produces an open neighbourhood V of y over which f is finite (statement lines 3267-3286). The proof chains three observations: the quasi-finiteness criterion for the codimension one case makes f quasi-finite at every point of the fibre over y; quasi-finiteness at a point makes the fibre discrete, hence quasi-compact as f is proper, hence finite; and the standard result that a proper morphism with finite fibre over a point is finite over some neighbourhood of that point finishes (proof lines 3288-3296). The claim is H2: three cited inputs in a fixed order, with the finiteness of the fibre as the step that converts discreteness into something the neighbourhood lemma can use.
